subject: Some questions about the hyper’s argumentsg

messages.author: 551aded02f98012e
messages.subject: Some questions about the hyper’s argumentsg
parts:
Hi all.

I know it's stupid,but I'm confused by the hyper's arguments:initial and fixed.I don't know what they're for and when do I need to change their default settings.

Thank you for any help in advance.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Some questions about the hyper’s argumentsg
parts:
Hi,

You can fix the hyper-parameter, e.g. to prevent overfitting. But shrinkage priors are better. See
https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic115.html#52_fix_(theta_1)_and_look_the_result
for examples doing both the fixing and the priors.

Note that when you fix the theta, you do not get it as part of the result (since you are not computing a posterior).

Kind regards,
Haakon

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Some questions about the hyper’s argumentsg
parts:
'initial' is its initial value, 'fixed=TRUE' say that this parameter is
considered as fixed, wheras 'fixed=FALSE" means that it will be
estimated. by construction, if you want to set a hyperparameter to a
certain value, then do

initial=A, fixed=TRUE


where 'A' is the value in the internal scale (\theta), check the
documentation.

H
